## Internship Timeline and Deliverables

To successfully complete the Approved Experience course, students must submit all required forms, reports, and evaluations on time. Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |
chunks.section: Internship Timeline and Deliverables

### EECE 500 internship duration (ECE)

**Department:** Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE)

**Question/topic:** How long is the EECE 500 (EECE500) internship course?

**Answer:** EECE 500 is the Approved Experience internship course for ECE students. The standard Approved Experience minimum is eight full weeks of approved training, typically 320 work hours. When an ECE student takes another summer course, additional duration and schedule limits may apply; see "Taking another summer course" below and confirm with the course team. The duration of the internship is separate from the length of the Final Training Report.

## Reporting after approval of multiple internship components

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** How should the Final Report cover two internships or an internship plus research?

**Answer:** For two internships, submit one Final Report that clearly separates and discusses each approved component. For a six-week internship plus two-week research arrangement, submit a separate research report in addition to the company internship report. This applies to every approved company-plus-research arrangement, including Dar Al-Handasah and other companies. Check Moodle for additional confirmed information based on your arrangement.

## Problems or changes during an internship

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** My assigned work is not technical or no longer matches the approved internship.

**Answer:** Report the issue immediately to the internship coordinator and, when applicable, the CDC. Do not wait until the internship ends because the experience may no longer meet the approved objectives.

**Question/topic:** My internship supervisor changed after I started.

**Answer:** Inform the coordinator immediately and provide the new supervisor's name, title, and email. The Notice of Arrival and, if necessary, the Proposal may need to be reopened or resubmitted.

Topic: MSFEA CDC Student Knowledge Base > Internship (Approved Experience Course) > Internship FAQs
### Internship FAQs
**Q: Does my Approved Experience internship have to be paid?**
A: No. The internship placement can be unpaid; a salary is not required for the Approved Experience internship. It must still satisfy the course's training and approval requirements. This is different from MSFEA CO-OP, whose work terms are paid.

**Q: When should I start applying for internships?**
A: Except for consulting internships, the CDC usually sends guidelines around the beginning of the academic year (October) for the following summer's internship. It is never too early to prepare — work on your CV and cover letter and explore options in advance.

Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > Combining two company internships
### Combining two company internships

**Question/topic:** Can two company internships be combined for EECE500, such as six weeks at one company and four at another, when I am not taking another summer course?

**Answer:** A combined arrangement requires prior written approval or petition; a six-plus-four company arrangement is not automatically accepted. Each internship must be documented and technically relevant, and the total approved duration must satisfy EECE500 requirements. After a six-week company placement, a second company internship must last at least four weeks, with or without another summer course. This gives at least ten company weeks for this route; it does not change the standard eight-week minimum for a single approved placement or the approved six-plus-two research route. Use the second-internship forms when instructed.
chunks.section: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > Combining two company internships

It is normally completed during the summer before the final year; the standard minimum is eight full weeks of approved training.

chunks.text:
## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.
chunks.section: Taking another summer course

Topic: MSFEA CDC Student Knowledge Base > Internship (Approved Experience Course) > Internship FAQs
### Internship FAQs
**Q: How do I apply through the CDC?**
A: When the CDC sends an offer, it will include instructions on how to apply — usually a Microsoft Form requiring your CV, cover letter, and academic transcript. After the deadline, the CDC forwards the candidate list to the employer for selection.

**Q: Can I apply to more than one internship offer at the same time?**
A: No. To give everyone a fair chance at CDC offers, you may only apply to one offer at a time. Avoid applying to offers you might later reject.

### Combining two company internships

**Question/topic:** Can two company internships be combined for EECE500, such as six weeks at one company and four at another, when I am not taking another summer course?

**Answer:** A combined arrangement requires prior written approval or petition; a six-plus-four company arrangement is not automatically accepted. Each internship must be documented and technically relevant, and the total approved duration must satisfy EECE500 requirements. After a six-week company placement, a second company internship must last at least four weeks, with or without another summer course. This gives at least ten company weeks for this route; it does not change the standard eight-week minimum for a single approved placement or the approved six-plus-two research route. ## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.

**Q: How do I apply through the CDC?**
A: When the CDC sends an offer, it will include instructions on how to apply — usually a Microsoft Form requiring your CV, cover letter, and academic transcript. After the deadline, the CDC forwards the candidate list to the employer for selection.

## Internship Timeline and Deliverables

To successfully complete the Approved Experience course, students must submit all required forms, reports, and evaluations on time. Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |

Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |

## Problems or changes during an internship

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** My assigned work is not technical or no longer matches the approved internship.

**Answer:** Report the issue immediately to the internship coordinator and, when applicable, the CDC. Do not wait until the internship ends because the experience may no longer meet the approved objectives.

**Question/topic:** My internship supervisor changed after I started.

**Answer:** Inform the coordinator immediately and provide the new supervisor's name, title, and email. The Notice of Arrival and, if necessary, the Proposal may need to be reopened or resubmitted.

## Combining two company internships (MECH)

**Department:** Mechanical Engineering (MECH)

A two-company arrangement needs prior department approval. Two separate four-week
company periods are not accepted for MECH; do not assume another split arrangement
will count without approval. The approved six-company-week plus two-week faculty
research route is a different arrangement, with its own engineering-work and
documentation conditions.
chunks.section: Combining two company internships (MECH)

chunks.text:
## Company internship plus research (MECH)

**Department:** Mechanical Engineering (MECH)

**Question/topic:** Can a MECH student combine a six-week company internship with two weeks of faculty research?

**Answer:** Six company weeks alone do not meet the standard eight-week minimum. A six-week company internship plus two weeks of approved faculty research may count for MECH when the research includes hands-on engineering work. Both components require approval and documentation.

Topic: MSFEA CDC Student Knowledge Base > Internship (Approved Experience Course) > Internship FAQs
### Internship FAQs
**Q: Does my Approved Experience internship have to be paid?**
A: No. The internship placement can be unpaid; a salary is not required for the Approved Experience internship. It must still satisfy the course's training and approval requirements. This is different from MSFEA CO-OP, whose work terms are paid.

**Q: When should I start applying for internships?**
A: Except for consulting internships, the CDC usually sends guidelines around the beginning of the academic year (October) for the following summer's internship. It is never too early to prepare — work on your CV and cover letter and explore options in advance.

### Application timeline (deadlines)

Students should apply to the CO-OP program at least one year before their intended
co-op start date. The application step is in July for the Summer + Fall track or

| 4 | Apply to advertised co-op positions via the CDC | Oct | May |

chunks.text:
## What CO-OP is

Cooperative education ("co-op") is a program in which students combine their
studies with one or more official **paid** work terms within their area of
study. The difference between a co-op work term and an internship is duration and
pay: internships are typically short (one or two months) and can be unpaid, while
co-op terms are longer and are paid. The **MSFEA co-op work term is a minimum of
6 months**, full-time and paid.
chunks.section: What CO-OP is

chunks.text:
## CO-OP FAQs
**Q: Is CO-OP associated with a course?**
A: Yes — the 3-credit Pass/Fail course **FEAA 500** (and **FEAA 500A** in the
second semester), which you register for every semester you are on co-op.

**Q: How many CO-OP opportunities can I apply to?**
A: Up to a **maximum of 3**, ranked by priority, but you can only accept and
confirm one.

**Q: Can I take other courses while on CO-OP?**
A: No, except possibly Final Year Project (FYP) or a 499 research course, if your
department allows it and it doesn't interfere with working hours.

## Motivation and benefits

- **For students:** a co-op lets students immerse themselves in an industry and
  better understand their field. A paid, extended placement builds a stronger
  sense of responsibility and makes the experience more meaningful. Research shows
  co-op participation increases student interest in learning and academic
  performance on return to campus, and leads to more satisfying career outcomes
  (Blair et al., 2004; Boudreau and Marx, 2019).

## What CO-OP is

Cooperative education ("co-op") is a program in which students combine their
studies with one or more official **paid** work terms within their area of
study. The difference between a co-op work term and an internship is duration and
pay: internships are typically short (one or two months) and can be unpaid, while
co-op terms are longer and are paid. The **MSFEA co-op work term is a minimum of
6 months**, full-time and paid.

## CO-OP FAQs
**Q: When can I go on CO-OP?**
A: In the 3rd or 4th year for Engineering/Graphic Design students, and the 4th or
5th year for Architecture students. You must return to campus for at least one
term afterward.

**Q: When should I apply to the CO-OP program?**
A: At least one year before your intended start date (you can begin applying in the
Spring of your 2nd year).

**Q: Do CO-OP course credits count toward my degree?**
A: This is decided by your department. You remain a full-time student during co-op
regardless.

## Internship Timeline and Deliverables

To successfully complete the Approved Experience course, students must submit all required forms, reports, and evaluations on time. Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |

Topic: Internship (Approved Experience) Report Templates and Rubrics > 2. Final Training Report Template (8–15 pages) > Final Approved Experience Report Rubric
### Final Approved Experience Report Rubric

| Criteria | Pass | Revision Required | Fail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Organization, Format, and Professional Writing | Report is professionally organized and formatted. Required sections are present. Writing is clear, coherent, and appropriate for a professional audience. Figures, tables, references, and appendices are effectively integrated. Minor errors do not affect readability. | Organization, formatting, writing quality, references, or supporting materials require improvement. Some required elements may be incomplete or inconsistently presented. | Report lacks required sections, is poorly organized, contains significant writing problems, or does not meet basic professional standards. |
| Description and Analysis of Experience | Clearly describes the organization, role, responsibilities, projects, activities, and contributions. Demonstrates meaningful participation and understanding through detailed examples and analysis. | Experience is described but important details, examples, or analysis are limited or incomplete. | Description is minimal, unclear, incomplete, or does not demonstrate meaningful participation. |
| Application of Engineering, Design, or Disciplinary Knowledge | Clearly demonstrates how disciplinary knowledge, methods, tools, technologies, analyses, or problem-solving approaches were applied. Provides specific and relevant examples. | Application of disciplinary knowledge is mentioned but lacks sufficient detail or explanation. | Little or no evidence of disciplinary knowledge being applied or understood. |
| Professional Learning and Growth | Demonstrates meaningful learning throughout the experience. Clearly explains skills developed, knowledge acquired, professional practices learned, and contributions to personal and professional growth. | Learning experiences are discussed but lack depth, reflection, or specific examples. | Little or no evidence of learning, growth, adaptation, or professional development. |
| Professional Practice and Broader Impact | Demonstrates awareness of professional considerations relevant to the experience, such as safety, sustainability, regulations, standards, quality, ethics, economic considerations, environmental impacts, societal impacts, or workplace responsibilities. Provides thoughtful reflection on the broader context of professional work. | Professional considerations are mentioned but discussion is superficial or lacks clear connection to the experience. | No meaningful discussion of professional practice or broader professional considerations. |

## AI use, similarity, and report revision
**Question/topic:** What is the maximum Turnitin similarity percentage?

**Answer:** The maximum similarity threshold is 20%. Cite sources properly and do not copy company descriptions or external text without quotation and reference.

**Question/topic:** Can AI be used only for grammar or wording?

**Answer:** Minor language assistance can still increase the AI-detection result. Review every sentence, disclose and cite AI use, and keep the technical content genuinely your own while remaining within the 25% limit.
chunks.section: AI use, similarity, and report revision

chunks.text:
## Progress Report deadline origin

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Is the Progress Report deadline based on my internship start date or the start of the semester?

**Answer:** Count internship weeks from your own approved internship start date. The Progress Report is due at the end of Week 4 unless Moodle announces a shared deadline. Follow the current course announcement when a common deadline is specified.
chunks.section: Progress Report deadline origin

chunks.text:
## AI use, similarity, and report revision

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can AI be used to write an internship report?

**Answer:** The report must be written in the student's own words. AI-generated text is limited to 25% and must be disclosed and cited. Students remain responsible for the accuracy and originality of the entire report.

**Question/topic:** What is the maximum AI percentage?

**Answer:** The maximum is 25%. A submission above the permitted limit may be considered unsatisfactory and returned for revision. The final submission must meet the course policy. Students should write independently and keep drafts and evidence of their work.
chunks.section: AI use, similarity, and report revision

## Proposal and Notice of Arrival timing

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** When are the internship Proposal and Notice of Arrival due, including if I have already started?

**Answer:** Complete the Proposal before beginning the approved internship and submit the Notice of Arrival during the first week of training. If you have already started and missed either step, contact the course coordinator promptly for instructions; do not assume the forms are waived or that a late submission is automatically accepted.
chunks.section: Proposal and Notice of Arrival timing

chunks.text:
## Moodle quiz access and attempts

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** I cannot access the internship Moodle quiz.

**Answer:** The quiz may remain restricted until all assigned lectures and recorded videos are completed or attempted. Complete the required resources and check again.

**Question/topic:** How many quiz attempts are allowed, or what happens if I do not reach the passing score?

**Answer:** Multiple attempts may be available so students can reach the required score. Follow the attempt settings on the current Moodle page. If the quiz is closed or no attempt remains, contact the coordinator.
chunks.section: Moodle quiz access and attempts

chunks.text:
## Student internship survey and employer-letter format
**Question/topic:** Can the employer simply state that I worked there?

**Answer:** No. A bare confirmation of attendance is not enough for the required employer completion/evaluation letter. It should state the actual internship start and end dates, the work and tasks completed, a brief evaluation, and the employer or supervisor's signature and stamp.

**Question/topic:** Does the document I received qualify as the required employer completion/evaluation letter?

**Answer:** An unseen document cannot be verified by the chatbot. To qualify, it must be an official employer or supervisor letter recording the actual start and end dates, work and tasks completed, a brief evaluation, and the required signature and stamp. Material prepared only for a presentation does not substitute for the letter. Ask the course team if an exceptional document needs approval.
chunks.section: Student internship survey and employer-letter format

Topic: MSFEA CDC Student Knowledge Base > Career Readiness Resources > Career+
### Career+

**Question/topic:** What is Career+? What does Career+ do? Tell me about Career+.

**Answer:** Career+ is an MSFEA career-development and certification initiative. It
helps students explore career options, align their career goals with their
aspirations, navigate career uncertainty, gain relevant skills, and begin career
planning from the start of their studies. Its certification paths recognize
development across four areas: academic work, applied experience, extracurricular
activities, and career readiness. To become certified, complete the requirements
for a specific Career+ path, apply for certification through the form linked on the
official page, and then receive feedback and certification. For the current paths,
requirements, documentation, and application form, use the official MSFEA CDC
Career+ page: https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/CareerPlus.aspx

### Internship FAQs
**Q: How do I apply through the CDC?**
A: When the CDC sends an offer, it will include instructions on how to apply — usually a Microsoft Form requiring your CV, cover letter, and academic transcript. After the deadline, the CDC forwards the candidate list to the employer for selection.

**Q: Can I apply to more than one internship offer at the same time?**
A: No. To give everyone a fair chance at CDC offers, you may only apply to one offer at a time. Avoid applying to offers you might later reject.

## Shared Final Report formatting and content
**Question/topic:** What should I write about acquiring and applying new knowledge?

**Answer:** Give a concrete example of knowledge or skills you needed for the internship, explain how you learned them and which resources or strategies helped, then describe how you applied them to your work and what resulted.

**Question/topic:** Do I need examples of engineering problem-solving in the Final Report?

**Answer:** Yes. Provide real examples or case studies showing how you applied engineering, science, and mathematics to complex engineering problems. Describe the challenges faced and solutions developed, and discuss relevant global, economic, environmental, and societal impacts using informed engineering judgment.

Topic: Internship (Approved Experience) Report Templates and Rubrics > 2. Final Training Report Template (8–15 pages) > Final Approved Experience Report Rubric
### Final Approved Experience Report Rubric

| Criteria | Pass | Revision Required | Fail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Organization, Format, and Professional Writing | Report is professionally organized and formatted. Required sections are present. Writing is clear, coherent, and appropriate for a professional audience. Figures, tables, references, and appendices are effectively integrated. Minor errors do not affect readability. | Organization, formatting, writing quality, references, or supporting materials require improvement. Some required elements may be incomplete or inconsistently presented. | Report lacks required sections, is poorly organized, contains significant writing problems, or does not meet basic professional standards. |
| Description and Analysis of Experience | Clearly describes the organization, role, responsibilities, projects, activities, and contributions. Demonstrates meaningful participation and understanding through detailed examples and analysis. | Experience is described but important details, examples, or analysis are limited or incomplete. | Description is minimal, unclear, incomplete, or does not demonstrate meaningful participation. |
| Application of Engineering, Design, or Disciplinary Knowledge | Clearly demonstrates how disciplinary knowledge, methods, tools, technologies, analyses, or problem-solving approaches were applied. Provides specific and relevant examples. | Application of disciplinary knowledge is mentioned but lacks sufficient detail or explanation. | Little or no evidence of disciplinary knowledge being applied or understood. |
| Professional Learning and Growth | Demonstrates meaningful learning throughout the experience. Clearly explains skills developed, knowledge acquired, professional practices learned, and contributions to personal and professional growth. | Learning experiences are discussed but lack depth, reflection, or specific examples. | Little or no evidence of learning, growth, adaptation, or professional development. |
| Professional Practice and Broader Impact | Demonstrates awareness of professional considerations relevant to the experience, such as safety, sustainability, regulations, standards, quality, ethics, economic considerations, environmental impacts, societal impacts, or workplace responsibilities. Provides thoughtful reflection on the broader context of professional work. | Professional considerations are mentioned but discussion is superficial or lacks clear connection to the experience. | No meaningful discussion of professional practice or broader professional considerations. |

## Internship Timeline and Deliverables

To successfully complete the Approved Experience course, students must submit all required forms, reports, and evaluations on time. Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |
chunks.section: Internship Timeline and Deliverables

### Internship FAQs
**Q: How do I apply through the CDC?**
A: When the CDC sends an offer, it will include instructions on how to apply — usually a Microsoft Form requiring your CV, cover letter, and academic transcript. After the deadline, the CDC forwards the candidate list to the employer for selection.

**Q: Can I apply to more than one internship offer at the same time?**
A: No. To give everyone a fair chance at CDC offers, you may only apply to one offer at a time. Avoid applying to offers you might later reject.

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** When are the internship Proposal and Notice of Arrival due, including if I have already started?

**Answer:** Complete the Proposal before beginning the approved internship and submit the Notice of Arrival during the first week of training. If you have already started and missed either step, contact the course coordinator promptly for instructions; do not assume the forms are waived or that a late submission is automatically accepted.

## Shared Final Report formatting and content
**Question/topic:** What should I write about acquiring and applying new knowledge?

**Answer:** Give a concrete example of knowledge or skills you needed for the internship, explain how you learned them and which resources or strategies helped, then describe how you applied them to your work and what resulted.

**Question/topic:** Do I need examples of engineering problem-solving in the Final Report?

**Answer:** Yes. Provide real examples or case studies showing how you applied engineering, science, and mathematics to complex engineering problems. Describe the challenges faced and solutions developed, and discuss relevant global, economic, environmental, and societal impacts using informed engineering judgment.

### Career+

**Question/topic:** What is Career+? What does Career+ do? Tell me about Career+.

**Answer:** Career+ is an MSFEA career-development and certification initiative. It
helps students explore career options, align their career goals with their
aspirations, navigate career uncertainty, gain relevant skills, and begin career
planning from the start of their studies. Its certification paths recognize
development across four areas: academic work, applied experience, extracurricular
activities, and career readiness. To become certified, complete the requirements
for a specific Career+ path, apply for certification through the form linked on the
official page, and then receive feedback and certification. For the current paths,
requirements, documentation, and application form, use the official MSFEA CDC
Career+ page: https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/CareerPlus.aspx

**Question/topic:** Can the employer simply state that I worked there?

**Answer:** No. A bare confirmation of attendance is not enough for the required employer completion/evaluation letter. It should state the actual internship start and end dates, the work and tasks completed, a brief evaluation, and the employer or supervisor's signature and stamp.

**Question/topic:** Does the document I received qualify as the required employer completion/evaluation letter?

**Answer:** An unseen document cannot be verified by the chatbot. To qualify, it must be an official employer or supervisor letter recording the actual start and end dates, work and tasks completed, a brief evaluation, and the required signature and stamp. Material prepared only for a presentation does not substitute for the letter. Ask the course team if an exceptional document needs approval.

## Internship Timeline and Deliverables

To successfully complete the Approved Experience course, students must submit all required forms, reports, and evaluations on time. Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |

## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.

**Question/topic:** Can two company internships be combined for EECE500, such as six weeks at one company and four at another, when I am not taking another summer course?

Each internship must be documented and technically relevant, and the total approved duration must satisfy EECE500 requirements. ## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.

## Finding an internship and acceptable work
**Question/topic:** What type of work is acceptable for the internship course?

**Answer:** The experience should be meaningful professional work related to the student's discipline and allow them to apply engineering, computing, design, analysis, or technical problem-solving skills. Work that is mainly unrelated business, finance, or administrative activity may not meet the course objectives. Department-specific limits and approval rules still apply.
chunks.section: Finding an internship and acceptable work

chunks.text:
## Shared Final Report formatting and content
**Question/topic:** What should I write about acquiring and applying new knowledge?

**Answer:** Give a concrete example of knowledge or skills you needed for the internship, explain how you learned them and which resources or strategies helped, then describe how you applied them to your work and what resulted.

**Question/topic:** Do I need examples of engineering problem-solving in the Final Report?

**Answer:** Yes. Provide real examples or case studies showing how you applied engineering, science, and mathematics to complex engineering problems. Describe the challenges faced and solutions developed, and discuss relevant global, economic, environmental, and societal impacts using informed engineering judgment.
chunks.section: Shared Final Report formatting and content

### Career+

**Question/topic:** What is Career+? What does Career+ do? Tell me about Career+.

**Answer:** Career+ is an MSFEA career-development and certification initiative. It
helps students explore career options, align their career goals with their
aspirations, navigate career uncertainty, gain relevant skills, and begin career
planning from the start of their studies. Its certification paths recognize
development across four areas: academic work, applied experience, extracurricular
activities, and career readiness. To become certified, complete the requirements
for a specific Career+ path, apply for certification through the form linked on the
official page, and then receive feedback and certification. For the current paths,
requirements, documentation, and application form, use the official MSFEA CDC
Career+ page: https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/CareerPlus.aspx

### Career+

**Question/topic:** What is Career+? What does Career+ do? Tell me about Career+.

**Answer:** Career+ is an MSFEA career-development and certification initiative. It
helps students explore career options, align their career goals with their
aspirations, navigate career uncertainty, gain relevant skills, and begin career
planning from the start of their studies. Its certification paths recognize
development across four areas: academic work, applied experience, extracurricular
activities, and career readiness. To become certified, complete the requirements
for a specific Career+ path, apply for certification through the form linked on the
official page, and then receive feedback and certification. For the current paths,
requirements, documentation, and application form, use the official MSFEA CDC
Career+ page: https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/CareerPlus.aspx

chunks.text:
## Internship Timeline and Deliverables

To successfully complete the Approved Experience course, students must submit all required forms, reports, and evaluations on time. Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |
chunks.section: Internship Timeline and Deliverables

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** My assigned work is not technical or no longer matches the approved internship.

**Answer:** Report the issue immediately to the internship coordinator and, when applicable, the CDC. Do not wait until the internship ends because the experience may no longer meet the approved objectives.

**Question/topic:** My internship supervisor changed after I started.

**Answer:** Inform the coordinator immediately and provide the new supervisor's name, title, and email. The Notice of Arrival and, if necessary, the Proposal may need to be reopened or resubmitted.

## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.

**Q: How do I apply through the CDC?**
A: When the CDC sends an offer, it will include instructions on how to apply — usually a Microsoft Form requiring your CV, cover letter, and academic transcript. After the deadline, the CDC forwards the candidate list to the employer for selection.

**Q: Can I apply to more than one internship offer at the same time?**

### Internship FAQs
**Q: Does my Approved Experience internship have to be paid?**
A: No. The internship placement can be unpaid; a salary is not required for the Approved Experience internship. It must still satisfy the course's training and approval requirements. This is different from MSFEA CO-OP, whose work terms are paid.

**Q: When should I start applying for internships?**
A: Except for consulting internships, the CDC usually sends guidelines around the beginning of the academic year (October) for the following summer's internship. It is never too early to prepare — work on your CV and cover letter and explore options in advance.

## Approved Experience course billing

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** How many credits is the internship course? Is it 1 credit or 90 credits? Is the internship course paid, how much should I pay for it, what does it cost, or what tuition or fee is charged?

**Answer:** The Approved Experience internship course itself is a 1-credit course and uses 1-credit billing. Separately, a student must have completed a minimum of 90 credits to be eligible to register for the internship course. The 90 completed credits are a registration eligibility requirement; they are not the credit value of the internship course or the number of credits billed for it.

## Internship Timeline and Deliverables

To successfully complete the Approved Experience course, students must submit all required forms, reports, and evaluations on time. Your internship file will only be considered complete after all required deliverables have been submitted, including the Final Training Report and required surveys/forms.

| Timeline | Deliverable | What You Need to Do | Submission Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| After the start of the Summer semester | Proposal of Approved Experience Form | Complete the internship proposal form before beginning your internship. | Moodle |
| During the first week of training | Notice of Arrival Form | Confirm that you have started your internship. | Moodle |
| During the internship | Professional Skills Requirement | Watch 3 recorded lectures on professional skills and engineering practice plus 3 internship experience videos from outstanding students, then complete the Moodle quiz with a minimum score of 75%. | Moodle |
| By the end of Week 4 | Progress Report | Submit a short report summarizing your internship experience and progress so far. | Moodle |
| Within 1 week after completing the internship | Final Training Report | Submit the final internship report following the template and guidelines posted on Moodle. | Moodle |
| At the end of the internship | Summary Sheet Form | Complete the online summary form. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Student Evaluation Form (all departments) | Complete the required student internship survey separately from the Summary Sheet and employer letter. | Online Form |
| At the end of the internship | Notice of Completion | Submit an official company letter confirming completion of your internship. | Upload / Department Submission |
| First 2 weeks of Fall semester (depending on department) | Final Presentation | Deliver your internship presentation (in person or recorded, depending on department requirements). | Department Submission |

It gives students a chance to apply classroom learning to real engineering and design challenges, gain professional experience and workplace skills, and explore career paths. It is normally completed during the summer before the final year; the standard minimum is eight full weeks of approved training.

**Q: Does passing FEAA 500 remove the department's Approved Experience requirement?**

### Final Approved Experience Report Rubric

| Criteria | Pass | Revision Required | Fail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Organization, Format, and Professional Writing | Report is professionally organized and formatted. Required sections are present. Writing is clear, coherent, and appropriate for a professional audience. Figures, tables, references, and appendices are effectively integrated. Minor errors do not affect readability. | Organization, formatting, writing quality, references, or supporting materials require improvement. Some required elements may be incomplete or inconsistently presented. | Report lacks required sections, is poorly organized, contains significant writing problems, or does not meet basic professional standards. |
| Description and Analysis of Experience | Clearly describes the organization, role, responsibilities, projects, activities, and contributions. Demonstrates meaningful participation and understanding through detailed examples and analysis. | Experience is described but important details, examples, or analysis are limited or incomplete. | Description is minimal, unclear, incomplete, or does not demonstrate meaningful participation. |
| Application of Engineering, Design, or Disciplinary Knowledge | Clearly demonstrates how disciplinary knowledge, methods, tools, technologies, analyses, or problem-solving approaches were applied. Provides specific and relevant examples. | Application of disciplinary knowledge is mentioned but lacks sufficient detail or explanation. | Little or no evidence of disciplinary knowledge being applied or understood. |
| Professional Learning and Growth | Demonstrates meaningful learning throughout the experience. Clearly explains skills developed, knowledge acquired, professional practices learned, and contributions to personal and professional growth. | Learning experiences are discussed but lack depth, reflection, or specific examples. | Little or no evidence of learning, growth, adaptation, or professional development. |
| Professional Practice and Broader Impact | Demonstrates awareness of professional considerations relevant to the experience, such as safety, sustainability, regulations, standards, quality, ethics, economic considerations, environmental impacts, societal impacts, or workplace responsibilities. Provides thoughtful reflection on the broader context of professional work. | Professional considerations are mentioned but discussion is superficial or lacks clear connection to the experience. | No meaningful discussion of professional practice or broader professional considerations. |

Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > Combining two company internships
### Combining two company internships

**Question/topic:** Can two company internships be combined for EECE500, such as six weeks at one company and four at another, when I am not taking another summer course?

**Answer:** A combined arrangement requires prior written approval or petition; a six-plus-four company arrangement is not automatically accepted. Each internship must be documented and technically relevant, and the total approved duration must satisfy EECE500 requirements. After a six-week company placement, a second company internship must last at least four weeks, with or without another summer course. This gives at least ten company weeks for this route; it does not change the standard eight-week minimum for a single approved placement or the approved six-plus-two research route. Use the second-internship forms when instructed.

### Applying to an internship found independently
If a student secures an internship on their own (not through the CDC), they must contact the CDC to confirm the company is approved. The CDC will then guide the student to either get the internship confirmed through the CDC, or petition their department directly.

### Internship FAQs
**Q: What is the minimum internship duration?**
A: To satisfy the approved experience requirement, the internship must be at least 8 weeks.

**Q: The company I'm applying to needs a letter (or a convention de stage) confirming the internship is required — who provides that?**
A: The CDC can provide a signed letter. Request it using the CDC letter request form: https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=Glu6x7ZB6UOhIG_2VK2hNxgNyBu3jyVItFyTXDeYtMVUODdKUjhTOTNPMEhJVFJTOExOUjZJWUZNUi4u

Topic: MSFEA CDC Student Knowledge Base > Career Readiness Resources > Career+
### Career+

**Question/topic:** What is Career+? What does Career+ do? Tell me about Career+.

**Answer:** Career+ is an MSFEA career-development and certification initiative. It
helps students explore career options, align their career goals with their
aspirations, navigate career uncertainty, gain relevant skills, and begin career
planning from the start of their studies. Its certification paths recognize
development across four areas: academic work, applied experience, extracurricular
activities, and career readiness. To become certified, complete the requirements
for a specific Career+ path, apply for certification through the form linked on the
official page, and then receive feedback and certification. For the current paths,
requirements, documentation, and application form, use the official MSFEA CDC
Career+ page: https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/CareerPlus.aspx

### Requesting a support letter

Request it through the CDC letter request form: https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=Glu6x7ZB6UOhIG_2VK2hNxgNyBu3jyVItFyTXDeYtMVUODdKUjhTOTNPMEhJVFJTOExOUjZJWUZNUi4u

The CDC will get back to you as soon as possible.

## Career Development Center (CDC) Internship Search and Postings

The MSFEA CDC office maintains strong relationships with employers and regularly updates job and internship postings. The CDC also supports students applying for competitive international opportunities. Students are strongly encouraged to:

- Stay in contact with the CDC.
- Regularly check internship postings.
- Attend the CDC information session at the beginning of the academic year.
chunks.section: Career Development Center (CDC) Internship Search and Postings

### Online Career Development Modules
The CDC offers asynchronous online modules (via Moodle) covering:
- **Resume and Cover Letter Writing** — preparing competitive CVs and cover letters
- **Interview Preparation** — practicing interview skills and strategies
- **Work Placement / Job Search** — identifying potential worksites and sources of opportunities, leveraging industry contacts
- **Workplace Environment and Skills** — preparing for success in the workplace

Topic: MSFEA CDC Student Knowledge Base > Internship (Approved Experience Course) > Internship FAQs
### Internship FAQs
**Q: How do I apply through the CDC?**
A: When the CDC sends an offer, it will include instructions on how to apply — usually a Microsoft Form requiring your CV, cover letter, and academic transcript. After the deadline, the CDC forwards the candidate list to the employer for selection.

**Q: Can I apply to more than one internship offer at the same time?**
A: No. To give everyone a fair chance at CDC offers, you may only apply to one offer at a time. Avoid applying to offers you might later reject.

Topic: Summer Training (Approved Experience) Guidelines > Securing an Internship Independently > If the Company Is Already Listed with the CDC
### If the Company Is Already Listed with the CDC

Being listed with the CDC does not itself approve your placement. Follow the
current CDC and Moodle process and obtain the required approval before starting.

- Submit an online petition requesting approval.
- Upload an official company letter that includes:
  - company letterhead
  - signature
  - internship duration
  - description of the training and expected work
